name: STM32L152RBT6A
title: Ultra-low-power Arm Cortex-M3 MCU, 32 to 128 KB Flash, 32 KB SRAM, 4 KB EEPROM, LCD, USB, ADC, DAC
summary: A family of ultra-low-power 32-bit Cortex-M3 microcontrollers running to 32 MHz from 1.65 V or 1.8 V to 3.6 V, with 32, 64 or 128 KB of Flash, up to 32 KB of SRAM and 4 KB of data EEPROM, with ECC on the Flash and EEPROM. Around the core sit a 12-bit 1 Msps ADC with up to 24 channels, a two-channel 12-bit DAC, two comparators, up to 20 touch-sensing channels, eight 16-bit timers, a calendar RTC, full-speed USB, three USARTs, two SPIs and two I2Cs; the STM32L152 adds an LCD driver for up to 8 x 40 segments. Standby draws 0.28 µA and Stop with RTC 1.38 µA. The STM32L152RBT6A is the LCD part in LQFP64 with 128 KB Flash and 32 KB SRAM, for -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: Arm Cortex-M3 with MPU, 32 kHz to 32 MHz, 1.25 DMIPS/MHz
Flash 32/64/128 KB, SRAM 16/32 KB, data EEPROM 4 KB; RBT6A: 128 KB / 32 KB / 4 KB
VDD 1.8 V to 3.6 V with BOR (1.65 V without BOR, D version); VDDA 1.8 V min with ADC or DAC
185 µA/MHz typ from Flash; 8.25 mA typ at 32 MHz, Range 1
Low-power run 10.9 µA; Stop 0.434 µA (1.38 µA with RTC); Standby 0.277 µA (1.11 µA with RTC) typ at 3.0 V
Stop 8.2 µs typ (MSI 4.2 MHz); Standby 58 µs typ
12-bit ADC 1 Msps, up to 24 channels; 2 × 12-bit DAC; 2 comparators; temperature sensor; VREFINT 1.224 V typ
HSE 1 to 24 MHz, HSI 16 MHz ±1 %, MSI 65.5 kHz to 4.2 MHz, LSI 37 kHz, LSE 32.768 kHz, PLL with 48 MHz for USB
37 / 51 / 83 by package, up to 73 5 V tolerant; ±8 mA (±20 mA relaxed)
USB 2.0 FS device, 3 × USART (4 Mbit/s), 2 × SPI (16 Mbit/s), 2 × I2C (SMBus/PMBus), LCD up to 8 × 40 (STM32L152)
LQFP48, UFQFPN48, LQFP64, TFBGA64, LQFP100, UFBGA100

notes: In xx the order code adds the package letter (H BGA, T LQFP, U UFQFPN) and the temperature digit (6: -40 °C to 85 °C, 7: -40 °C to 105 °C); a trailing D marks the 1.65 V version without BOR and TR tape and reel. STM32L152RBT6A: LCD device, LQFP64, 128 KB Flash, 32 KB RAM, -40 °C to 85 °C.
STM32L151 devices have no LCD controller.

operation.text: The STM32L151x6/8/B-A and STM32L152x6/8/B-A are generation-A ultra-low-power Cortex-M3 MCUs. The 152 adds the LCD controller, the 151 has none. The letter after the subfamily gives the pin count (C 48, R 64, V 100) and the next digit the Flash (6 32 KB, 8 64 KB, B 128 KB).

ARM Cortex-M3 at up to 32 MHz (33.3 DMIPS, 1.25 DMIPS/MHz), with an 8-region memory protection unit plus an optional background region. The NVIC handles 45 maskable interrupt channels besides the 16 core lines, with 16 priority levels, tail-chaining and late-arrival handling.

VDD (1.65 V to 3.6 V) feeds the I/Os and the internal regulator through the VDD pins. VDDA/VSSA (1.65 V to 3.6 V, 1.8 V minimum with the ADC) feed the ADC, reset blocks, RC oscillators and PLL, and are tied to VDD and VSS.

operation.topic: Power-on, BOR and the D version
operation.text: Power-on/power-down reset is combined with a brownout reset. The standard version has BOR active at power-on and runs from 1.8 V to 3.6 V; the D version has no BOR at power-on and runs from 1.65 V. Once the POR threshold is passed the option bytes load and can change the BOR level or switch BOR off for good, after which 1.65 V is the minimum for either version. Without BOR at power-up, VDD reaches 1.65 V at least 1 ms after leaving the POR region. Start-up takes about 3.3 ms with BOR at power-up and about 1 ms without. No external reset circuit is needed: the part stays in reset below VPOR/PDR or VBOR.

Five BOR thresholds from 1.8 V to 3 V are set in the option bytes. The PVD compares VDD/VDDA with one of seven software-selected levels from 1.85 V to 3.05 V, about 200 mV apart, and can interrupt when the supply falls below or rises above it. VREFINT can be switched off automatically in Stop to save current.

Three modes: main regulator in Run; low-power regulator in Stop and in both low-power modes (run and sleep); power-down in Standby, where the core domain is unpowered and RAM and registers are lost; only the wakeup logic, IWDG, RTC, LSI, LSE and RCC_CSR are kept.

The core voltage follows the needed speed: Range 1 (VCORE 1.8 V, VDD 1.71 V to 3.6 V) up to 32 MHz; Range 2 (1.5 V, full VDD range) up to 16 MHz; Range 3 (1.2 V, full range) up to 4 MHz, from the MSI only. Above 16, 8 or 2.1 MHz respectively the Flash needs one wait state.

Sleep stops only the CPU. Low-power run executes from Flash or SRAM on the MSI at range 0 or 1 (131 kHz max) with the low-power regulator. Low-power sleep is Sleep with the low-power regulator, for example with a timer running at 32 kHz. Stop keeps RAM and registers, stops all core-domain clocks and the PLL, MSI, HSI and HSE, optionally keeps the RTC on LSE or LSI, and wakes in about 8 µs on any EXTI line: the 16 external lines, the PVD, either comparator (with VREFINT on), RTC alarms, tamper, timestamp or wakeup, or USB wakeup. Standby powers off the core domain and wakes in about 60 µs on NRST, an IWDG reset, an RTC event or a rising edge at any of the three WKUP inputs. The RTC, IWDG and their clocks keep running in Stop and Standby.
BOOT0 and BOOT1 (PB2) pick Flash, system memory or embedded RAM at start-up. The system-memory bootloader reprograms the Flash over USART1 or USART2 (ST application note AN2606).

System clock sources: HSE crystal 1 MHz to 24 MHz, HSI 16 MHz RC (±1 % factory trimmed) and MSI, seven ranges from 65.5 kHz to 4.2 MHz with current proportional to speed (down to 750 nA), trimmable to ±0.5 % against the LSE. The PLL runs from HSE or HSI and gives a dedicated 48 MHz for USB, which needs the HSE crystal as source. LSE 32.768 kHz and LSI 37 kHz clock the RTC and LCD (HSE can also), and the LSI clocks the IWDG and can be measured against the HSI. After reset the CPU runs on the MSI at 2.1 MHz. The clock security system switches to HSI if the HSE fails. MCO outputs an internal clock. AHB, APB1 and APB2 run at up to 32 MHz.

BCD calendar with sub-seconds, 12/24 h and automatic month lengths, two alarms and a periodic wakeup from 120 µs to 36 hours that works from Stop and Standby. Calibration uses a 512 Hz output and digital compensation, and a 50/60 Hz mains reference (RTC_REFIN) can correct it. Sub-second on-the-fly updates allow network synchronization; a timestamp input records an event. Twenty 32-bit backup registers (80 bytes) are cleared by a tamper event on one of three filterable tamper pins.

Each GPIO can be input (floating, pull-up or pull-down), push-pull or open-drain output, or alternate function, and all are high-current capable. The configuration can be locked. GPIO toggling reaches 16 MHz on the AHB. The EXTI has 23 edge detectors: 16 lines shared by up to 83 GPIOs and 7 lines from the RTC, PVD, USB and comparators; it catches pulses shorter than one APB2 clock.

Up to 32 KB of SRAM at CPU speed with no wait state; 32, 64 or 128 KB of Flash, 4 KB of data EEPROM and option bytes, all with ECC. Read-out protection: level 0 none; level 1 blocks Flash access with debug connected or boot from RAM; level 2 disables debug and boot from RAM permanently. Write protection has 4 KB granularity, and PCROP blocks data-bus reads of user Flash.

Seven-channel DMA moving data between memories and peripherals in any direction, with circular buffers, a hardware request per channel plus software trigger, and independent source and destination sizes; serves SPI, I2C, USART, timers and ADC.

STM32L152 only. Drives up to 8 commons and 44 segments, at most 320 display dots. An internal step-up converter keeps contrast independent of VDD; when it is off, VLCD supplies the LCD. Duty static, 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 or 1/8; bias static, 1/2, 1/3 or 1/4; phase inversion; up to 8 blinking dots; double-buffered display RAM; runs in Stop. Unused COM and SEG pins remain GPIOs. Intermediate bias rails can be decoupled on PB2, PB12/PE11 and PB0/PE12.

One 12-bit ADC with up to 24 external channels, single or scan conversion, DMA, an analog watchdog on one or more channels, timer triggers for regular and injected groups, and a low-power mode with auto-shutdown so it runs at full speed while the CPU runs slowly. Conversions reach 1 Msps from 2.4 V and 500 ksps from 1.8 V; below 1.8 V the ADC and DAC do not work.

TSENSE gives a voltage linear in temperature on ADC_IN16. Each device is calibrated at 30 °C and 110 °C, with the raw ADC readings stored read-only in system memory (TS_CAL1, TS_CAL2); uncalibrated, it suits relative measurements only.

VREFINT is a bandgap reference for the ADC and comparators on ADC_IN17; its value, measured per part at 3 V, is stored as VREFINT_CAL and lets VDD be computed when no external VREF+ exists. It is available on VREF_OUT (PB0 or PB1) through a low-power buffer that sources up to 1 µA.

Two 12-bit buffered channels (resistor string plus non-inverting amplifier), left or right aligned data, synchronized update, noise and triangle generation, independent or simultaneous conversion, DMA with underrun interrupt, and external triggers from eight timer update events. Reference is VREF+. The output buffer can be bypassed.

Two comparators share bias and reference. COMP1 has a fixed threshold; COMP2 is rail-to-rail with fast or slow mode and a threshold from the DAC, an I/O, VREFINT or 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4 of VREFINT. Both wake the part from Stop and can be combined as a window comparator.
Firmware routes I/Os to the TIM2, TIM3 and TIM4 input captures and internal analog signals to the ADC, COMP1, COMP2 and VREFINT.

Up to 20 capacitive sensing channels in 10 analog I/O groups, by surface charge transfer: the sensor is charged and its charge moved into a sampling capacitor until a threshold is reached. GPIOs, timers and the analog groups do the acquisition with few external parts; ST's STMTouch library supports it.

TIM2, TIM3, TIM4: 16-bit up/down counters with four capture/compare/PWM channels, DMA, quadrature encoder and hall-sensor inputs. TIM9 (two channels), TIM10 and TIM11 (one channel) can be clocked from the LSE for time bases independent of the CPU clock. All general-purpose timers synchronize through the timer link. TIM6 and TIM7 are basic timers mainly for DAC triggers. SysTick is a 24-bit down-counter. The IWDG (12-bit, 8-bit prescaler) runs from the 37 kHz LSI and keeps going in Stop and Standby; the WWDG (7-bit) runs from the main clock with an early-warning interrupt.

Two I2C interfaces, multimaster and slave, standard and fast mode, dual 7-bit slave addresses, 7- and 10-bit master addressing, hardware CRC, DMA and SMBus 2.0/PMBus. SDA and SCL are not genuine open-drain pins: set to open-drain, the PMOS to VDD is switched off but still present.
Three USARTs to 4 Mbit/s with CTS/RTS flow control, ISO 7816 smartcard, IrDA SIR, LIN master/slave and DMA.
Two SPIs to 16 Mbit/s as master or slave, full or half duplex, eight master baud settings from a 3-bit prescaler, 8- or 16-bit frames, hardware CRC for SD/MMC and DMA.

Full-speed (12 Mbit/s) USB device with configurable endpoints and suspend/resume, clocked at 48 MHz from the PLL on the HSE crystal. VDD is at least 3.0 V for USB levels, and D+ (USB_DP) is pulled up by 1.5 kΩ to 3.0 V to 3.6 V.
A CRC unit computes a 32-bit CRC with a fixed polynomial, used for example for Flash integrity checks under EN/IEC 60335-1. Each device has a 96-bit unique ID.

SWJ-DP combines JTAG and serial wire debug: JTMS/SWDIO and JTCK/SWCLK are shared and a sequence on JTMS switches between them. A JTAG fuse can disable the port for good. The ETM streams instruction and data trace on TRACECLK and TRACED0 to TRACED3 to an external trace port analyzer.

Voltages are referred to VSS. Min and max are guaranteed in production at TA = 25 °C and TAmax unless a note says characterization, design or simulation; characterized limits are mean ±3σ. Typical values are at 25 °C and VDD = 3.0 V and are not tested; typical ADC accuracy is mean ±2σ (95 % of parts). Pin measurements use a 50 pF load.

Run figures use code equivalent to Dhrystone 2.1. All I/O are in analog input mode and peripherals off unless listed; Flash wait states, 64-bit access and prefetch are set for the frequency and range; with peripherals on fAPB1 = fAPB2 = fAHB. With the PLL on, its input is HSI 16 MHz or HSE 16 MHz in bypass. Max figures at VDD = VDDA = 3.6 V, typical at 3.0 V.
Wakeup times are measured on the MSI. Sleep wakes on the clock in use before; Stop wakes on the MSI in its previous range; Standby wakes on the MSI at 2.1 MHz.
In HSE bypass the oscillator is off and OSC_IN takes an external clock as a standard GPIO input, up to 32 MHz.

Crystal or ceramic resonator 1 MHz to 24 MHz. CL1 and CL2 are high-quality high-frequency ceramics, typically 5 pF to 25 pF and usually equal, chosen so their series value plus about 10 pF of pin and board capacitance matches the crystal's load. Keep resonator and capacitors close to the pins (ST application note AN2867).
32.768 kHz crystal with CL1 and CL2 of 5 pF to 15 pF, usually equal. To keep them at or below 15 pF, use a crystal with CL ≤ 7 pF and never a 12.5 pF one. Keep the parts close to the pins.

Each I/O sinks or sources up to ±8 mA, and up to ±20 mA with relaxed VOL/VOH. The sum of sourced I/O current plus the maximum Run current must stay within ΣIVDD, and the sum sunk plus Run current within ΣIVSS.

Injection beyond the rails is avoided in normal use. In characterization, failure means ADC error over 5 LSB TUE, leakage on neighbouring pins outside –5 µA/+0 µA, or a functional fault. A Schottky diode from pin to ground protects analog pins that may see negative current.
Every I/O meets both CMOS and TTL levels. FT pins accept 5.5 V with VDD ≥ 2.0 V and 5.25 V below, as long as their pull resistors are off.
NRST has a permanent pull-up of 45 kΩ typical. 0.1 µF right at the pin protects against parasitic resets; an external driver must take the pin below VIL(NRST) max.
fPCLK1 must be at least 2 MHz for standard mode, 4 MHz for fast mode, and a multiple of 10 MHz for exactly 400 kHz.
VREF+ draws 700 µA max while sampling and for the first two conversion clocks, and 300 µA max for the rest of the 12-cycle conversion.
Decouple as in the power supply scheme, with the 100 nF parts good-quality ceramics as close to the chip as possible. The pad adds about 7 pF to the board's parasitic capacitance at an analog input.

EMS is tested with ESD per IEC 61000-4-2 on all pins and fast transient bursts per IEC 61000-4-4 through 100 pF on VDD and VSS, while the part toggles two LEDs. Failures such as unexpected reset or program-counter corruption can be reproduced by holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 s; software can be hardened against them (ST application note AN1015). Emission is measured per IEC 61967-2.

ESD: positive then negative pulses one second apart on every pin combination, sample size 3 parts × (n + 1) supply pins. Latch-up: supply overvoltage and current injection on every I/O, on six parts, per JESD78A.

Maximum power dissipation is set by TJmax. At TA = 85 °C (suffix 6) or 105 °C (suffix 7) PD max is 606 mW (UFQFPN48), 444 mW (LQFP64), 435 mW (LQFP100), 364 mW (LQFP48), 339 mW (UFBGA100) and 308 mW (TFBGA64); at lower ambient more is allowed while TJ stays within TJmax.
The top side carries the product identification, a date code (year and week), a revision code and a pin 1 mark. Parts marked ES or E are engineering samples, not qualified for production.
